title.zh: 卷一百五十一 列傳第七十六 關董袁趙竇
title.en: Volume 151 Biographies 76: Guan, Dong, Yuan, Zhao, Dou˚ Guāndǒngyuánzhàodòu
title.raw: 卷一百五十一 列傳第七十六 關董袁趙竇 Volume 151 Biographies 76: Guan, Dong, Yuan, Zhao, Dou˚ Guāndǒngyuánzhàodòu

sentences.zh: 關董袁趙竇

translations.literal: Guan, Dong, Yuan, Zhao, Dou
translations.idiomatic: Guan, Dong, Yuan, Zhao, and Dou

sentences.zh: 關播，字務元，衛州汲人。

translations.literal: Guan Bo, styled Wuyuan, was a native of Ji in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo, whose courtesy name was Wuyuan, came from Ji in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 及進士第。

translations.literal: He attained the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 鄧景山節度青齊、淮南，再署幕府。

translations.literal: When Deng Jingshan was military commissioner of Qingji and Huainan, [Guan] was twice appointed to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jingshan governed Qingji and Huainan, and Guan served twice on his staff.

sentences.zh: 遷右補闕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the post of Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 與神策軍使王駕鶴為姻家，元載惡之，出為河南兵曹參軍事，數試屬縣，政異等。

translations.literal: He was related by marriage to Wang Jiahe, commissioner of the Shence Army; Yuan Zai hated him and had him sent out as military affairs adjutant in Henan; he was repeatedly assigned to trial subordinate counties, and his administration was rated in the top class.
translations.idiomatic: He was connected by marriage to Wang Jiahe of the Shence Army; Yuan Zai took a dislike to him and had him posted as military affairs adjutant in Henan. Assigned repeatedly to oversee subordinate counties, his governance was rated in the highest class.

sentences.zh: 陳少遊鎮浙東、淮南，表為判官，攝滁州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chen Shaoyou governed Zhedong and Huainan, [Chen] memorialized him as administrative aide and acting prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou, who held Zhedong and Huainan, recommended him as administrative aide and acting prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 李靈耀叛，少遊屯淮上，所在盜賊蝟奮，播儲貲力，給軍興，人無愁苦。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled, Shaoyou encamped on the Huai; everywhere bandits surged like hedgehogs bristling; Bo mustered stored goods and strength to supply military needs, and the people knew no distress.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rose in rebellion, Shaoyou held the Huai line while bandits flared up everywhere. Bo drew on stored supplies and local strength to meet military needs, and the people were spared hardship.

sentences.zh: 楊綰、常袞皆善播，引為都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Yang Guan and Chang Gun both favored Bo and recommended him as Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guan and Chang Gun both took a liking to Bo and had him appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 德宗初，湖南峒賊王國良驚剽州縣，不可制，詔播宣輯，因得請事，對殿中。

translations.literal: In the early Dezong reign, the cave bandit Wang Guoliang of Hunan raided and plundered prefectures and counties beyond control; an edict ordered Bo to go pacify and reconcile them; he thereby obtained an audience to report on affairs in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Dezong's reign, the Hunan cave-bandit Wang Guoliang terrorized prefectures and counties beyond control. An edict sent Bo to pacify the region, and he secured an audience in the hall to report on the mission.

sentences.zh: 帝問政治之要，播曰：「為政之本，要得有道賢人乃治。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked about the essentials of governing; Bo said: "The foundation of administering the state is that one must obtain worthy men who possess the Way—only then is there good government."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what mattered most in governing the realm. Bo replied, "At the root of statecraft lies finding worthy men who truly follow the Way; only then can the realm be well ruled."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕比下詔求賢才，又遣使黜陟，搜逮所遺，須能者用之，若何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Recently I have issued edicts seeking talented men, and also sent commissioners to dismiss and promote officials, searching out those overlooked—when capable men appear they shall be used—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have lately issued edicts seeking talent and sent commissioners to promote and dismiss officials, combing for anyone overlooked—when the capable appear, they are to be used. What more is needed?"

sentences.zh: 播曰：「陛下雖求賢，又使舉薦，然止得求名文辭士，焉有有道賢人肯奉牒丐舉選邪？」

translations.literal: Bo said: "Though Your Majesty seeks worthies and also has people recommend them, yet one only obtains men who seek fame and excel in literary composition—how could there be worthy men who possess the Way willing to accept credentials and beg to enter the selection process?"
translations.idiomatic: Bo said, "Your Majesty may seek worthies and order recommendations, yet you still end up with men who chase reputation and polish their prose. What man of true worth who follows the Way would accept a summons and beg his way into the selection process?"

sentences.zh: 帝悅，曰：「卿姑去，還當更議。」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said: "You may withdraw for now; we shall discuss this again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said, "Withdraw for now; we shall take this up again."

sentences.zh: 播且言：「奉詔平賊，有如不受命，臣請發州兵剪定之。」

translations.literal: Bo then said: "In obeying the edict to pacify the bandits, if I am not obeyed I request to mobilize provincial troops and cut them down and settle them."
translations.idiomatic: Bo added, "In carrying out the edict to pacify the bandits, if my orders are not obeyed I ask leave to raise provincial troops and cut them down once and for all."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Very well."

sentences.zh: 及還，再遷給事中。

translations.literal: When he returned he was again promoted to Supervising Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned he was promoted again to Supervising Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 故事，諸司甲庫，以令史直曹，刓脫為奸。

translations.literal: By precedent, the armor depots of the various offices had clerk-duty officers who shaved away [funds] and became corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, the armor depots of the various ministries were staffed by clerks on rotating duty, who shaved off funds and turned corrupt.

sentences.zh: 播悉易以士人，時韙其法。

translations.literal: Bo entirely replaced them with scholar-officials; at the time people praised his reform.
translations.idiomatic: Bo replaced them all with scholar-officials, and contemporaries praised the reform.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝求宰相，盧杞雅知播韋柔可制，因從容言播材任宰相，其儒厚可鎮浮動。

translations.literal: The emperor sought a chief minister; Lu Qi had long known that Bo and Wei Rou were controllable, and thus spoke at leisure that Bo's talents suited the chief ministership, that his Confucian steadiness could calm volatile affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was looking for a chief minister. Lu Qi had long known that Bo and Wei Rou were men he could control, and remarked at leisure that Bo's talents fitted the chief ministership and that his Confucian steadiness could steady volatile times.

sentences.zh: 乃拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，政一決於杞。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Manager of Affairs of the Secretariat and Chancellery; all policy decisions rested with Qi alone.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and chief minister, but every policy decision rested with Lu Qi alone.

sentences.zh: 嘗論事帝前，播意不可，避坐欲有所言，杞目禁輒止，退讓播曰：「以君寡言，故至此，奈何欲開口爭事邪！」

translations.literal: Once when discussing affairs before the emperor, Bo thought something unacceptable; he left his seat intending to speak, but Qi glared and forbade him, stopping him; afterward Qi told Bo: "Because you are sparing of words you have come to this—why do you wish to open your mouth and dispute affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, while discussing policy before the emperor, Bo found something unacceptable and rose from his seat to speak, but Lu Qi glared him into silence. Afterward Qi told him, "You were brought here because you keep quiet—why do you want to open your mouth and argue over policy?"

sentences.zh: 播即喑畏毋敢與。

translations.literal: Bo immediately went mute with fear and dared not contest with him.
translations.idiomatic: Bo fell silent in fear and no longer dared dispute with him.

sentences.zh: 時李元平、陶公達、張愻、劉承誡率輕薄子，遊播門下，能侈言誕計，以功名自喜。

translations.literal: At the time Li Yuanping, Tao Gongda, Zhang Su, and Liu Chengjie led frivolous youths who wandered in Bo's gate, able to boast grand schemes and reckoning on merit and fame for self-satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Yuanping, Tao Gongda, Zhang Su, and Liu Chengjie led a crowd of frivolous young men who haunted Bo's household, boasting grand schemes and basking in dreams of merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 播謂皆將相材，數請帝用之。

translations.literal: Bo said they were all ministerial and general material and repeatedly asked the emperor to employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Bo declared them all material for generals and ministers and repeatedly urged the emperor to employ them.

sentences.zh: 元平本宗室疏裔，好論兵，鄙天下士大夫無可者，人人怨疾之。

translations.literal: Yuanping was originally a distant scion of the imperial clan, fond of discussing military affairs, despising all scholar-officials under heaven as not his match—everyone resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanping was a distant offshoot of the imperial clan who loved to talk of war and held every scholar-official under heaven beneath contempt; everyone resented him.

sentences.zh: 李希烈叛，帝以汝州據賊沖，刺史疲軟不勝任，播盛稱元平，帝召見，拜左補闕。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled, the emperor considered Ruzhou situated on the rebel thrust, its prefect wearied and soft and unfit for the post; Bo lavishly praised Yuanping; the emperor summoned and met him and appointed him Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, the emperor saw Ruzhou lying on the rebel line of advance and its prefect as too weak for the post. Bo lavishly praised Yuanping; the emperor summoned him and appointed him Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 不數日，檢校吏部郎中，兼汝州別駕，知州事。

translations.literal: Within a few days he was made acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Vice Prefect of Ruzhou, managing prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was made acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Vice Prefect of Ruzhou, with charge of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 元平始至，募工築郛浚隍，希烈陰使亡命應募，凡內數百人，元平不寤。

translations.literal: When Yuanping first arrived he recruited workers to build the outer wall and dredge the moat; Xilie secretly sent fugitives to enlist; several hundred were inside [the wall], and Yuanping did not realize it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanping first arrived he recruited laborers to build the outer wall and dredge the moat. Xilie secretly sent fugitives to enlist; several hundred were inside the works, and Yuanping never caught on.

sentences.zh: 賊遣將李克誠以精騎薄城，募者內應，縛元平馳見希烈，遺矢於地。

translations.literal: The rebel sent the general Li Kecheng with crack cavalry to press the city; the recruits responded from within, bound Yuanping and hurried to show him to Xilie, who let droppings fall to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent Li Kecheng with elite cavalry against the city. The recruits rose inside, bound Yuanping, and rushed him before Xilie, who fouled himself on the ground.

sentences.zh: 希烈以其眇小，無髯，戲克誠曰：「使爾取元平，乃以其子來邪？」

translations.literal: Xilie, because he was tiny and beardless, jested to Kecheng: "Did I send you to capture Yuanping, only for you to bring his son?"
translations.idiomatic: Xilie, seeing how small and beardless he was, joked to Kecheng, "Did I send you to take Yuanping, or only to bring me his son?"

sentences.zh: 因嫚罵曰：「盲宰相使汝當我，何待我淺邪！」

translations.literal: He then jeered and reviled: "The blind chief minister sent you to handle me—why did you treat me so lightly!"
translations.idiomatic: He then mocked and reviled him: "The blind chief minister sent you to deal with me—why do you take me so lightly!"

sentences.zh: 偽署御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was falsely appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a false appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 播聞詫曰：「元平事濟矣！」

translations.literal: When Bo heard of it he said in astonishment: "Yuanping's affair has succeeded!"
translations.idiomatic: When Bo heard the news he exclaimed in astonishment, "Yuanping's mission has succeeded!"

sentences.zh: 謂必覆賊而建功也，左右笑之。

translations.literal: He meant that [Yuanping] would surely overthrow the rebels and establish merit; those at his side laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: He meant that Yuanping would surely overthrow the rebels and win glory; those around him laughed.

sentences.zh: 無何，偽署為宰相，有告其貳者，元平斷一指自誓。

translations.literal: Before long [Xilie] falsely appointed him chief minister; there were reports of his disloyalty, and Yuanping cut off a finger to swear loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xilie gave him a false appointment as chief minister. When reports of disloyalty reached him, Yuanping cut off a finger to swear his faith.

sentences.zh: 公達等以元平屈賊，皆廢不用。

translations.literal: Gongda and the others, because Yuanping had submitted to the rebels, were all dismissed and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Gongda and the others, because Yuanping had submitted to the rebels, were all cast aside and never employed.

sentences.zh: 播從幸奉天。

translations.literal: Bo followed in attendance when the emperor fled to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Bo accompanied the emperor when he fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 盧杞、白誌貞已貶而播猶執政，議者不平，遂罷為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Although Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen had already been demoted, Bo still held office as chief minister; commentators were not reconciled, so he was dismissed to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen had already been demoted, Bo still held power as chief minister, and critics would not accept it; he was therefore removed to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 韋倫等曰：「宰相不善謀，使天子播越，尚可尚書邪？」

translations.literal: Wei Lun and others said: "The chief minister did not plan well and made the Son of Heaven wander in hardship—can he still be Minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun and others said, "The chief minister planned poorly and drove the Son of Heaven into exile—how can he still hold a ministry?"

sentences.zh: 相與泣諸朝。

translations.literal: They wept together before the court.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together at court over the matter.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知刪定使。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Director of the Revision Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was put in charge of the Revision Commission.

sentences.zh: 初，上元中，詔擇古名將十人配享武成廟，如十哲侑孔子。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Shangyuan era, an edict chose ten celebrated generals of antiquity to receive sacrificial companionship in the Martial Accomplishment Temple, like the Ten Sages accompanying Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Shangyuan era, an edict chose ten celebrated generals of antiquity to receive sacrificial companionship in the Martial Accomplishment Temple, on the model of the Ten Sages who accompany Confucius.

sentences.zh: 播奏：「太公，古賢臣，今其下稱亞聖。

translations.literal: Bo memorialized: "The Duke of Zhou was an ancient worthy minister; now beneath him he is called Sub-Sage.
translations.idiomatic: Bo memorialized, "The Duke of Zhou was an ancient worthy minister, yet those installed beneath him are now called Sub-Sages.

sentences.zh: 孔子十哲，皆當時弟子，今所配年世不同，請罷之。」

translations.literal: Confucius's Ten Sages were all disciples of his time; those now installed are of different ages—please abolish this."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's Ten Sages were all disciples of his own day, whereas those now installed belong to different ages. I ask that this practice be abolished."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，檢校尚書右仆射，持節送鹹安公主降回鶻，虜人重其清。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenyuan era he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and, bearing credentials, escorted Princess Xian'an to marry into the Uyghurs; the barbarians respected his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and, bearing credentials, escorted Princess Xian'an to marry into the Uyghurs; the foreigners respected his integrity.

sentences.zh: 還，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was transferred to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 以太子少師致仕，斥賣車騎，闔門不嬰外事。

translations.literal: He retired as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, sold off his carriages and mounts, and closed his gate, not troubling himself with outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, sold off his carriages and mounts, and shut his gate against outside affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十九，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-nine; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-nine and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 始，希烈死，或言元平雖屈賊，然有謀不克發，乃貸死流珍州。

translations.literal: Initially, after Xilie died, some said that though Yuanping had submitted to the rebels he had had a plot that could not be carried out, and his death sentence was commuted to exile to Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xilie's death, some argued that although Yuanping had submitted to the rebels he had harbored a plot that never came off, and his death sentence was commuted to exile in Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 會赦還，住剡中，觀察使皇甫政殺其侄以發帝怒，遂流死賀州。

translations.literal: When a general amnesty brought him back, he lived in Shanzhong; the surveillance commissioner Huangfu Zheng killed his nephew to provoke the emperor's anger, and he was exiled to die in Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty brought him back, and he settled in Shanzhong. The surveillance commissioner Huangfu Zheng killed his nephew to stir the emperor's wrath, and Yuanping was exiled to die in Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 董晉，字混成，河中虞鄉人。

translations.literal: Dong Jin, styled Huncheng, was a native of Yuxiang in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jin, whose courtesy name was Huncheng, came from Yuxiang in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 擢明經。

translations.literal: He was selected through the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 肅宗幸彭原，上書行在，拜秘書省校書郎，待制翰林。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong reached Pengyuan, [Dong] submitted a memorial to the traveling court and was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat, attending at the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong reached Pengyuan, Dong submitted a memorial to the traveling court and was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat, with attendance duty at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 出從淮南崔圓府為判官。

translations.literal: He went out to serve on the staff of Cui Yuan, military commissioner of Huainan, as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as administrative aide on the staff of Cui Yuan, military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 還朝，累遷祠部郎中。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court, he rose in stages to Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，李涵持節送崇徽公主於回紇，署晉判官。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, Li Han, bearing credentials, escorted Princess Chonghui to the Uyghurs and appointed Jin as his administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era Li Han, bearing credentials, escorted Princess Chonghui to the Uyghurs and appointed Jin his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 回紇恃有功，見使者倨，因問：「歲市馬而唐歸我賄不足，何也？」

translations.literal: The Uyghurs relied on their merit and met the envoy arrogantly, and therefore asked: "Each year we sell horses yet Tang returns our bribes insufficiently—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs, relying on their past service, received the envoy arrogantly and asked, "Each year we sell you horses, yet Tang returns our gifts in insufficient measure—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 涵懼，未及對，數目晉，晉曰：「我非無馬而與爾為市，為爾賜者不已多乎？

translations.literal: Han was afraid and had not yet replied when he repeatedly glanced at Jin; Jin said: "It is not that we lack horses and trade with you as a market—we have already given you many gifts, have we not?
translations.idiomatic: Han was afraid and had not yet answered when he kept glancing at Jin. Jin said, "It is not that we lack horses and must trade with you as in a market—the gifts we have already bestowed on you are not few, are they?

sentences.zh: 爾之馬歲五至，而邊有司數皮償貲。

translations.literal: Your horses come five times a year, yet border offices count pelts to compensate the price.
translations.idiomatic: Your horses arrive five times a year, yet border offices count pelts to set the compensation price.

sentences.zh: 天子不忘爾勞，敕吏無得問，爾反用是望我邪？

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven does not forget your labor and orders officials not to press the matter—yet you use this to expect more from us?
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has not forgotten your service and has ordered officials not to press the matter—yet you use this as grounds to demand more from us?

sentences.zh: 諸戎以我之爾與也，莫敢確。

translations.literal: All the border peoples take what we give you as a standard—none dares dispute.
translations.idiomatic: All the frontier peoples take what we give you as the standard—none dares dispute it.

sentences.zh: 爾父子寧，畜馬蕃，非我則誰使！」

translations.literal: You father and son would not be at peace or raise many horses if not for us—who else would let you!"
translations.idiomatic: You and your father would not live in peace or raise so many horses if not for us—who else would allow it!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆南面拜，不敢有言。

translations.literal: The assembly all bowed facing south and dared make no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly bowed facing south and dared say nothing more.

sentences.zh: 還，遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，授太府卿。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne, he was granted the Directorship of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, he was appointed Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 不旬日，為左散騎常侍，兼御史中丞，知臺事。

translations.literal: Within ten days he was made Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, managing the bureau's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was made Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, with charge of the Censorate's affairs.

sentences.zh: 出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，遣兵攻之，晉棄華走行在。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled he sent troops to attack; Jin abandoned Hua and fled to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled he sent troops against Huazhou; Jin abandoned the prefecture and fled to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 改國子祭酒，宣慰恒州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Chancellor of the National University and sent as Commissioner for Pacification and Comfort to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Chancellor of the National University and sent as Commissioner for Pacification and Comfort to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 還至河中而李懷光反，晉說之曰：「朱泚為臣而背其君，茍得誌，於公何有？

translations.literal: Returning as far as Hezhong, Li Huaiguang rebelled; Jin persuaded him: "Zhu Ci was a subject yet betrayed his lord—even if he had his wish, what would he do for you?
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reached Hezhong just as Li Huaiguang rebelled. Jin urged him, "Zhu Ci was a subject who betrayed his lord—even if he had his way, what would that mean for you?

sentences.zh: 且公位太尉，泚雖寵公，亦無以加。

translations.literal: Moreover your rank is Grand Marshal; though Ci might favor you, he cannot add to it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you hold the rank of Grand Marshal; even if Ci favored you, he could add nothing to your standing.

sentences.zh: 彼不能事君，能以臣事公乎？

translations.literal: He cannot serve the lord—can he serve you as a subject?
translations.idiomatic: He cannot serve his lord—how could he serve you as a subject?

sentences.zh: 公能事彼，而有不能事君乎？

translations.literal: If you can serve him, is there one you cannot serve as lord?
translations.idiomatic: If you could serve him, would there be any lord you could not serve?

sentences.zh: 公敵賊有餘力，若襲取之，清宮以迎天子，雖有大惡猶將掩焉，如公則誰敢議？」

translations.literal: You have surplus strength against the rebels; if you strike and seize them, clear the palace to welcome the Son of Heaven—even for great wickedness it can still be covered; as for you, who would dare discuss it?"
translations.idiomatic: You still have more than enough strength to defeat the rebels. If you strike and seize them and clear the palace to welcome the Son of Heaven, even great past faults can be covered over—and who, in your case, would dare raise them?"

sentences.zh: 懷光喜且泣，晉亦泣。

translations.literal: Huaiguang was pleased and wept, and Jin wept as well.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was moved to joy and tears, and Jin wept as well.

sentences.zh: 又語其將卒，皆拜。

translations.literal: He also addressed his officers and men, and all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed Huaiguang's officers and men, and all bowed in assent.

sentences.zh: 故懷光雖偃蹇，亦不助泚。

translations.literal: Therefore though Huaiguang was overbearing and difficult, he still did not aid Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, though Huaiguang remained overbearing and difficult, he still did not aid Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 帝還京師，遷左金吾衛大將軍，改尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Jin was promoted Grand General of the Left Golden Guard and changed to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Jin was promoted Grand General of the Left Golden Guard and reassigned as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是時，右丞元琇為韓滉排笮得罪，滉勢振朝廷。

translations.literal: At the time the Right Vice Director Yuan Xuan had been impeached and punished by Han Huang for petty faults; Huang's power shook the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Right Vice Director Yuan Xuan had been impeached and punished on petty charges by Han Huang, whose power now dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 晉見宰相，誦元琇非罪，士大夫壯其節。

translations.literal: When Jin saw the chief ministers he declaimed Yuan Xuan's innocence; scholar-officials admired his fortitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin met the chief ministers he spoke out on Yuan Xuan's innocence, and scholar-officials admired his moral courage.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，以門下侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan he was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Concurrent Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan he was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 方竇參得君，裁可大事不關咨晉，晉循謹無所駁異。

translations.literal: Just then Dou Can had won the ruler's trust; he could decide great affairs without consulting Jin; Jin followed cautiously and offered no objections.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Dou Can had won the emperor's trust and could decide major affairs without consulting Jin; Jin followed cautiously and raised no objections.

sentences.zh: 參欲以其侄申為吏部侍郎，諷晉以聞。

translations.literal: Can wished to make his nephew Shen Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and hinted to Jin to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Can wished to make his nephew Shen Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and hinted that Jin should report it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「無乃參迫卿為之邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily: "Surely Can is pressing you to do this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily, "Surely Dou Can pressured you into this?"

sentences.zh: 晉謝，具道所以然。

translations.literal: Jin apologized and fully explained how matters stood.
translations.idiomatic: Jin apologized and explained in full how the matter had arisen.

sentences.zh: 帝即問參過失，晉無敢隱，由是參罷宰相。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately asked about Can's faults; Jin dared hide nothing, and thereby Can was removed as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately asked about Can's faults; Jin concealed nothing, and Can was therefore removed as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 晉惶恐，上疏固辭位。

translations.literal: Jin was fearful and submitted a memorial firmly declining the post.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was alarmed and submitted a memorial firmly declining his post.

sentences.zh: 九年，罷為禮部尚書，以兵部尚書為東都留守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was dismissed to Minister of Rites and made Minister of War as Eastern Capital Defender.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was removed to Minister of Rites and appointed Minister of War as Eastern Capital Defender.

sentences.zh: 會宣武李萬榮病且死，詔晉檢校尚書左仆射、同中書門下平章事，為宣武節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: When Xuanwu's Li Wanrong fell ill and was near death, an edict appointed Jin acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Chief Minister as Xuanwu's deputy military commissioner, managing military commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Wanrong of Xuanwu fell gravely ill and was near death, an edict appointed Jin acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and chief minister as deputy military commissioner of Xuanwu, with charge of the commission's affairs.

sentences.zh: 萬榮死，鄧惟恭總其軍。

translations.literal: When Wanrong died, Deng Weigong took command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanrong died, Deng Weigong took overall command of his army.

sentences.zh: 晉受命，不召兵，惟幕府騶傔從之，即日上道。

translations.literal: When Jin received the command he did not summon troops—only his staff's mounted escorts and attendants followed him; that very day he set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin received the appointment he summoned no troops—only the mounted escorts and attendants of his staff accompanied him, and that same day he set out on the road.

sentences.zh: 至鄭，逆者不至，人勸止以觀便宜，晉不聽，直造汴。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhengzhou, the welcoming party did not come; people urged him to stop and observe how things stood; Jin would not listen and went straight to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhengzhou no welcoming party appeared; people urged him to halt and see how matters stood, but Jin would not listen and went straight on to Bian.

sentences.zh: 及郊，惟恭始出迎謁。

translations.literal: At the suburbs, only then did Weigong come out to welcome and do obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban greeting ground Weigong at last came out to welcome him and perform obeisance.

sentences.zh: 既入，即委以軍政，無所改更，眾服晉有體，莫測其謀。

translations.literal: Once inside he immediately entrusted military and civil administration to him, altering nothing; the multitude admired that Jin had proper bearing, and none could fathom his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside he immediately entrusted civil and military administration to Weigong without changing a thing; the men admired Jin's bearing and could not fathom his design.

sentences.zh: 始，惟恭謀代萬榮，故不遣吏以疑晉，令不敢入。

translations.literal: Initially Weigong had plotted to replace Wanrong and therefore did not send officials to receive Jin, making him dare not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong had originally plotted to replace Wanrong and therefore sent no officials to receive Jin, hoping to make him afraid to enter.

sentences.zh: 及晉至情得，則鞅鞅不能平。

translations.literal: Once Jin arrived and the situation was clear, [Weigong] was discontented and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin arrived and the situation was clear, Weigong was discontented and could not settle his mind.

sentences.zh: 汴士素驕怙亂，嘗介勇士伏幕下，早暮番休，晉一罷之。

translations.literal: The men of Bian had long been arrogant and relied on disorder; they often posted warriors to lie in ambush beneath the curtain, rotating morning and evening—Jin abolished this at once.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Bian had long been arrogant and accustomed to disorder; they often posted warriors to lie in ambush beneath the command tent, rotating in shifts morning and evening—Jin abolished the practice at once.

sentences.zh: 惟恭乃結大將相裏重晏等謀亂，晉覺之，殺其黨，械送惟恭京師。

translations.literal: Weigong then joined with the great generals Xiangli Chongyan and others to plot rebellion; Jin discovered it, killed their faction, and sent Weigong in fetters to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong then conspired with the senior generals Xiangli Chongyan and others to raise a revolt. Jin uncovered the plot, executed the conspirators, and had Weigong bound and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝錄其縶李乃勞，貸死流汀州。

translations.literal: The emperor recorded his capture and credited the merit, commuted death, and exiled him to Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took account of his capture, spared his life, and banished him to Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝恐晉儒軟，詔拜汝州刺史陸長源為司馬，以佐晉。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing Jin was too soft as a Confucian scholar, issued an edict appointing Ruzhou prefect Lu Changyuan as military adjutant to assist Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Jin was too mild and bookish, the emperor appointed Lu Changyuan, prefect of Ruzhou, as army adjutant to assist him.

sentences.zh: 晉謙願儉簡，事多循仍，故軍粗安。

translations.literal: Jin was modest and willing to be frugal and simple; affairs mostly followed established ways, so the army was roughly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was modest and inclined to frugality and simplicity, and most matters followed precedent, so the army remained broadly at peace.

sentences.zh: 長源持法峭刻，數欲更張舊事，晉初許之，已而悉罷不用。

translations.literal: Changyuan enforced the law harshly and sharply, repeatedly wishing to overhaul old practices; Jin at first assented, but afterward abandoned them all and did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan applied the law with harsh severity and repeatedly sought to overhaul old practices. Jin initially agreed, but in the end set every proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 以財賦委孟叔度，叔度為人佻侻，軍中惡之。

translations.literal: He entrusted finances and taxes to Meng Shudu; Shudu was frivolous by nature, and the army detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Financial affairs were entrusted to Meng Shudu, a man of frivolous character whom the troops despised.

sentences.zh: 晉在軍凡五年，卒，年七十六，贈太傅，謚曰恭惠。

translations.literal: Jin was with the army altogether five years, then died at seventy-six; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor, with the posthumous title Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Jin spent five years with the army, then died at seventy-six. He was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Gonghui.

sentences.zh: 晉為相也，五月朔，天子會朝，公卿在廷，侍中贊群臣賀，竇參攝中書令，當傳詔，疾作，公卿相顧，未有詔，晉從容進曰：「攝中書令臣參病不能事，臣請代參事。」

translations.literal: When Jin served as chief minister, on the first day of the fifth month the Son of Heaven held court; the nobles and ministers were in the hall; the attendant-in-chief led the ministers in congratulation; Dou Can, acting as Director of the Secretariat, was to transmit the edict but fell ill; the nobles and ministers looked at one another—there was no edict—whereupon Jin calmly stepped forward and said, "Acting Director of the Secretariat, Minister Dou, is ill and cannot serve; your subject requests to serve in Dou's place.
translations.idiomatic: While Jin was chief minister, on the first day of the fifth month the emperor held court with all the nobles and ministers present. The attendant-in-chief was leading the officials in congratulation when Dou Can, acting Director of the Secretariat, fell ill before he could transmit the edict. The court officials looked at one another in confusion until Jin calmly stepped forward and said, "Acting Director of the Secretariat Minister Dou is ill and unable to serve. I request to take his place.

sentences.zh: 南面宣致詔詞，進退甚詳。

translations.literal: Facing south he proclaimed and delivered the edict; his advance and withdrawal were very proper.
translations.idiomatic: Facing south, he proclaimed the edict with meticulous propriety in every movement.

sentences.zh: 金吾將軍沈房有期喪，公除，常服入閤，帝疑以問晉，對曰：「故事，朝官期以下喪，服絁縵，不復衣淺色，南班亦如之。」

translations.literal: Golden Guard General Shen Fang had period mourning; when mourning was publicly ended he entered the inner hall in regular dress; the emperor, suspicious, questioned Jin, who replied, "By precedent, when court officials have mourning below the full term, they wear bordered coarse hemp and no longer wear light colors; the southern rank officials do likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Guard General Shen Fang was in period mourning. When his mourning was publicly ended, he entered the inner hall in ordinary dress. The emperor questioned Jin about it, and Jin replied, "By precedent, court officials in mourning below the full term wear bordered coarse hemp and no longer wear light-colored garments; officials of the outer ranks follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 又問晉冠冕之制，對曰：「古者服冠冕，以佩玉節步。

translations.literal: The emperor again asked Jin about the regulations for caps and ceremonial robes, and he replied, "In antiquity one wore cap and robe and used jade pendants to regulate one's pace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked Jin about the regulations governing caps and ceremonial dress. Jin replied, "In antiquity, one wore cap and robe and used jade pendants to regulate one's pace.

sentences.zh: 堂上接武，堂下布武，君前趨進而已。

translations.literal: On the hall one shortened the steps; below the hall one took full steps; before the ruler one merely quickened forward—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall one shortened the steps; below the hall one took full steps; before the ruler one merely quickened forward—that was all.

sentences.zh: 今或奔走以致顛仆。

translations.literal: Now some run and thereby fall.
translations.idiomatic: Nowadays some break into a run and fall as a result.

sentences.zh: 在式，朝臣皆綾袍，五品而上金玉帶，所以盡飾以奉上。

translations.literal: According to the regulations, court ministers all wore silk robes; from the fifth rank upward they wore gold-and-jade belts—this was to adorn themselves fully in serving the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Under court regulations, ministers wore silk robes, and from the fifth rank upward they wore gold-and-jade belts, fully adorned in service to the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 故漢尚書郎含香，老萊采服，君父一也。

translations.literal: Hence the Han Ministry attendant bearing incense and Laolai in colored dress: ruler and father are one.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Han Ministry attendant bearing incense and Laolai in colored dress—the ruler and one's father are one and the same.

sentences.zh: 若然，服絁縵，亦非禮也。」

translations.literal: If so, wearing bordered coarse hemp is also not ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, then wearing bordered coarse hemp is likewise improper."

sentences.zh: 帝然其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with what he said.

sentences.zh: 詔入閤官毋趨走，期以下喪不得以慘服會，令群臣衣本品綾袍、金玉帶，自晉而復。

translations.literal: An edict was issued that officials entering the inner hall must not run; those in mourning below the full term might not attend court in mourning dress; all ministers were ordered to wear silk robes and gold-and-jade belts of their proper rank—a practice restored from Jin's time.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: officials entering the inner hall must not run; those in mourning below the full term might not attend court in mourning dress; and all ministers were to wear silk robes and gold-and-jade belts appropriate to their rank—a practice restored at Jin's urging.

sentences.zh: 子溪，字惟深，亦擢明經，三遷萬年令。

translations.literal: His son Xi, courtesy name Weishen, also passed the Mingjing examination and was thrice promoted to magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi, courtesy name Weishen, also passed the Mingjing examination and rose through three promotions to become magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 討王承宗也，擢度支郎中，為東道行營糧料使。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong was being suppressed, he was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Revenue and made grain-supply commissioner for the Eastern Expedition field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Wang Chengzong he was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Revenue and appointed grain-supply commissioner for the Eastern Expedition field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 坐盜軍貲，流封州，至長沙，賜死。

translations.literal: Convicted of embezzling military funds, he was exiled to Fengzhou; upon reaching Changsha he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of embezzling military funds, he was exiled to Fengzhou; upon reaching Changsha he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 子居中，善詩，為張籍所稱。

translations.literal: His son Juzhong was skilled in poetry and was praised by Zhang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Juzhong was a gifted poet and won praise from Zhang Ji.

sentences.zh: 陸長源者，吳人，字泳。

translations.literal: Lu Changyuan was a man of Wu, courtesy name Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Changyuan was a native of Wu, courtesy name Yong.

sentences.zh: 祖餘慶，天寶中為太子詹事，有清譽。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuqing served as Household Chief of the Crown Prince during the Tianbao era and had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuqing served as Household Chief of the Crown Prince during the Tianbao era and enjoyed a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 長源贍於學，始辟昭義薛嵩幕府，嵩侈汰，常從容規切。

translations.literal: Changyuan was well versed in learning; he was first recruited into the staff of Xue Song of Zhaoyi; Song was extravagant and wasteful, and Changyuan often tactfully admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in scholarship, Changyuan first entered the staff of Xue Song of Zhaoyi. Song was extravagant and wasteful, and Changyuan often admonished him with tact.

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「非君安能為此。」

translations.literal: Song said, "If not for you, who could do this?
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "If not for you, who else could speak to me this way?

sentences.zh: 歷建、信二州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Jian and Xin.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in succession as prefect of Jian and Xin.

sentences.zh: 韓滉兼領江淮轉運使，辟署兼御史中丞，以為副。

translations.literal: Han Huang, while concurrently serving as transport commissioner for the Huai and Jiang circuits, recruited him with the concurrent title of Censor-in-Chief and made him his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Huang concurrently served as transport commissioner for the Huai and Jiang circuits, he recruited Changyuan as deputy censor-in-chief and made him his assistant.

sentences.zh: 入遷都官郎中，復出汝州刺史。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director in the Bureau of Punishments, then went out again as prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Director in the Bureau of Punishments, then returned to the provinces as prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 遂徙宣武，政皆出司馬。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Xuanwu, and all government affairs issued from the military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Xuanwu, where all administrative affairs were decided by the army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 初，欲峻法繩驕兵，為晉所持，不克行。

translations.literal: At first he wished to restrain the arrogant soldiers with stern law, but Jin held him back and he could not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: At first he wished to restrain the arrogant troops with strict law, but Jin held him back and the plan could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 而判官楊凝、孟叔度等又苛細，叔度淫縱，數入倡家調笑嬉褻。

translations.literal: Yet the adjutants Yang Ning and Meng Shudu and others were also harsh and petty; Shudu was licentious and unrestrained, repeatedly entering brothels to jest and indulge in lewd sport.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the adjutants Yang Ning and Meng Shudu and others were also harsh and petty. Shudu was dissolute and unrestrained, often visiting brothels for lewd jest and sport.

sentences.zh: 晉有所偷弛，長源輒裁正之。

translations.literal: Whenever Jin was lax, Changyuan would at once correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jin slackened discipline, Changyuan promptly corrected him.

sentences.zh: 晉卒，長源總留後事，大言曰：「將士久慢，吾且以法治之！」

translations.literal: When Jin died, Changyuan took charge of rear affairs and declared loudly, "The officers and soldiers have long been negligent—I shall govern them by law!
translations.idiomatic: When Jin died, Changyuan assumed charge of rear affairs and declared, "The officers and soldiers have long been negligent—I shall bring them under the law!

sentences.zh: 眾始懼。

translations.literal: The men first grew afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were finally afraid.

sentences.zh: 軍中請出帑帛為晉制服，不許。

translations.literal: The army requested treasury silk and cloth to make mourning garments for Jin; he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The army asked that treasury silk and cloth be issued for mourning garments for Jin, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 固請，止給其直。

translations.literal: They pressed the request; he would only give the cash value.
translations.idiomatic: When they pressed the request, he would only pay the cash equivalent.

sentences.zh: 叔度希望又償直以鹽，乃高鹽直，賤帛估，人得鹽二斤，舉軍大怒。

translations.literal: Shudu, hoping to profit, again compensated the cash value with salt; he raised the price of salt and cheapened the valuation of cloth, so each man received only two jin of salt, and the whole army was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Shudu, hoping to profit, again paid the cash value in salt. He inflated the price of salt and undervalued the cloth, so each man received only two jin of salt, and the entire army erupted in fury.

sentences.zh: 或勸長源曰：「故事，有大變則厚賜於軍，軍乃安。」

translations.literal: Someone advised Changyuan, "By precedent, when there is a great change one gives generous gifts to the army, and then the army is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised Changyuan, "By precedent, when there is a great upheaval one bestows generous gifts upon the army, and only then does the army settle down.

sentences.zh: 長源曰：「異時河北賊以錢買戍卒，取旌節，吾不忍為。」

translations.literal: Changyuan said, "In former times the rebels of Hebei bought garrison soldiers with money to seize the commander's insignia—I cannot bear to do that."
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan said, "In former times the Hebei rebels bought off garrison soldiers with money to seize the commander's insignia. I cannot bring myself to do that."

sentences.zh: 眾怒益甚。

translations.literal: The crowd's anger grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: The troops' anger grew even fiercer.

sentences.zh: 長源性剛不適變，又不為備。

translations.literal: Changyuan's nature was rigid and unsuited to change, and he made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan was rigid by nature, ill suited to changing circumstances, and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 才八日，軍亂，殺長源及叔度等，食其肉，放兵大掠。

translations.literal: After only eight days the army mutinied, killed Changyuan and Shudu and the others, ate their flesh, and the soldiers looted on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: After only eight days the army mutinied, killed Changyuan, Shudu, and the others, devoured their flesh, and the troops ran wild in a great pillage.

sentences.zh: 死之日，有詔拜節度使，遠近嗟悵，贈尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: On the day he died there was an edict appointing him military governor; near and far sighed in sorrow; he was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died an edict arrived appointing him military governor. Near and far mourned him with sighs, and he was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 長源好諧易，無威儀，而清白自將。

translations.literal: Changyuan liked easy humor and had no imposing bearing, yet kept himself pure and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan was easygoing and fond of humor, without imposing bearing, yet he kept himself pure and upright.

sentences.zh: 去汝州，送車二乘，曰「吾祖罷魏州，有車一乘，而圖書半之，吾愧不及先人」雲。

translations.literal: When he left Ruzhou, two carriages saw him off; he said, "When my grandfather left Weizhou he had one carriage, and books filled half of it—I am ashamed that I cannot match my forebears," he said.
translations.idiomatic: When he left Ruzhou, two carriages saw him off. He said, "When my grandfather left Weizhou he had one carriage, and books filled half of it. I am ashamed that I cannot measure up to my forebears."

sentences.zh: 長源死，監軍俱文珍密召宋州刺史劉全諒使總後務。

translations.literal: When Changyuan died, the army overseer Ju Wenzhen secretly summoned Songzhou prefect Liu Quanliang to take charge of rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Changyuan's death, the army overseer Ju Wenzhen secretly summoned Songzhou prefect Liu Quanliang to take charge of rear affairs.

sentences.zh: 全諒至，其夜軍復亂，殺大將及部曲五百人乃定。

translations.literal: When Quanliang arrived, that night the army mutinied again; only after killing great generals and retainers numbering five hundred did it settle.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanliang arrived, the army mutinied again that same night. Order was restored only after five hundred senior officers and their retinues had been killed.

sentences.zh: 帝即詔全諒檢校工部尚書、宣武節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor at once appointed Quanliang acting Minister of Works and military governor of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately appointed Quanliang acting Minister of Works and military governor of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 全諒，始名逸淮，至是賜名，本懷州武涉人也。

translations.literal: Quanliang was originally named Yihuai; at this time he was granted his new name; he was a native of Wushe in Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanliang had originally been named Yihuai; at this time he was granted his new name. He was a native of Wushe in Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 父客奴，以行戍留籍幽州，事平盧軍，以材力顯。

translations.literal: His father Kenü, through frontier garrison service, remained registered in Youzhou; he served the Pinglu army and distinguished himself by strength and ability.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kenü, through frontier garrison service, remained registered in Youzhou. He served in the Pinglu army and won distinction for his strength and ability.

sentences.zh: 開元中，室韋首領段普洛數苦邊，節度使薛楚玉使客奴單騎襲之，斬首以歸。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era the Shiwei chieftain Duan Pulu repeatedly harassed the border; military governor Xue Chuyu sent Kenü alone on horseback to raid him, beheaded him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era the Shiwei chieftain Duan Pulu repeatedly harassed the frontier. Military governor Xue Chuyu sent Kenü alone on horseback to raid him, beheaded him, and returned.

sentences.zh: 興卒伍，拜左驍衛將軍，為遊奕使。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks and was appointed General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and made patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to be appointed General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and patrol commissioner.

sentences.zh: 性謹樸，數戰有功。

translations.literal: By nature he was cautious and plain; he fought many battles with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Cautious and plain by nature, he fought in many battles and won merit.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，詔以平盧節度副使呂知誨為使。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, an edict made Pinglu deputy military governor Lü Zhihui the military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, an edict appointed Pinglu deputy military governor Lü Zhihui as military governor.

sentences.zh: 賊遣韓朝旸誘之，知誨即降，賊害安東副都護馬靈察。

translations.literal: The rebels sent Han Chaoyang to entice him; Zhihui at once surrendered, and the rebels killed Andong deputy protector Ma Lingcha.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent Han Chaoyang to win him over. Zhihui surrendered at once, and the rebels killed Andong deputy protector Ma Lingcha.

sentences.zh: 客奴不平，與諸將共殺知誨，遣使與安東將王玄誌相聞。

translations.literal: Kenü was indignant; with the generals he jointly killed Zhihui and sent an envoy to communicate with Andong general Wang Xuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Indignant, Kenü joined the other generals in killing Zhihui and sent an envoy to establish contact with Andong general Wang Xuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 天寶十五載，以客奴為柳城郡太守，攝御史大夫、平盧節度使，賜名正臣；

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianbao, Kenü was made prefect of Liucheng Commandery, acting Censor Grandee and Pinglu military governor, and granted the name Zhengchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianbao, Kenü was made prefect of Liucheng Commandery, acting Censor Grandee and Pinglu military governor, and granted the name Zhengchen.

sentences.zh: 以玄誌為安東副大都護。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi was made Andong deputy grand protector.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanzhi was made Andong deputy grand protector.

sentences.zh: 正臣遣使道海至平原，與太守顏真卿相結。

translations.literal: Zhengchen sent an envoy by sea to Pingyuan and allied with prefect Yan Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchen sent an envoy by sea to Pingyuan and formed an alliance with prefect Yan Zhenqing.

sentences.zh: 真卿喜，以子為質而歸貲糧焉，且請出師。

translations.literal: Zhenqing was pleased; he sent his son as hostage and returned funds and grain, and also requested that troops be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing was delighted. He sent his son as a hostage, returned funds and grain, and asked that troops be sent out.

sentences.zh: 未至，而真卿棄平原，乃還。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Zhenqing abandoned Pingyuan, and so they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Zhenqing had abandoned Pingyuan, and so they turned back.

sentences.zh: 因襲范陽，為史思明所敗，奔還，玄誌冘殺之。

translations.literal: They then raided Fanyang, were defeated by Shi Siming, fled back, and Xuanzhi, in fear, killed Zhengchen.
translations.idiomatic: They then raided Fanyang, were defeated by Shi Siming, fled back, and Xuanzhi, fearing reprisal, had Zhengchen killed.

sentences.zh: 全諒事劉玄佐為牙將，以勇果善騎射為玄佐厚禮。

translations.literal: Quanliang served Liu Xuanzuo as a yamen guard general; for courage, decisiveness, and skill in mounted archery, Xuanzuo treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Quanliang served Liu Xuanzuo as a yamen guard general. Xuanzuo treated him generously for his courage, decisiveness, and skill in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 累兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He repeatedly also held the concurrent post of Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly held the concurrent post of censor-in-chief as well.

sentences.zh: 及玄佐子士寧代立，疑宋州刺史翟良佐不附己，揚言行部，至則以全諒代之，故汴將士多歸心焉。

translations.literal: When Xuanzuo's son Shining succeeded him, suspecting that Songzhou prefect Zhai Liangzuo did not attach himself to him, he announced that he would inspect the prefectures; upon arrival he replaced Liangzuo with Quanliang, so the officers and soldiers of Bian mostly gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzuo's son Shining succeeded him, he suspected that Songzhou prefect Zhai Liangzuo was not loyal to him. Shining announced that he would tour the prefectures, and upon reaching Songzhou replaced Liangzuo with Quanliang, so the officers and soldiers of Bian largely came to favor him.

sentences.zh: 視事凡八月卒，贈尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: He governed altogether eight months and died; he was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He governed for eight months and died. He was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 軍中立韓弘代節度云。

translations.literal: The army established Han Hong to replace him as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The army established Han Hong to replace him as military governor.

sentences.zh: 袁滋，字德深，蔡州朗山人，陳侍中憲之後。

translations.literal: Yuan Zi, courtesy name Deshen, was a man of Langshan in Caizhou and a descendant of Chen attendant-in-chief Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zi, courtesy name Deshen, was a native of Langshan in Caizhou and a descendant of Chen attendant-in-chief Xian.

sentences.zh: 強學博記。

translations.literal: He studied hard and remembered broadly.
translations.idiomatic: He studied hard and had a broad memory.

sentences.zh: 少依道州刺史元結，讀書自解其義，結重之。

translations.literal: In youth he relied on Daozhou prefect Yuan Jie; reading books, he understood their meaning on his own, and Jie valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he relied on Daozhou prefect Yuan Jie. Reading books, he grasped their meaning on his own, and Jie valued him.

sentences.zh: 後客荊、郢間，起學廬講授。

translations.literal: Later he sojourned between Jing and Ying, built a study hall, and lectured.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sojourned between Jing and Ying, built a study hall, and lectured there.

sentences.zh: 建中初，黜陟使趙贊薦於朝，起處士，授試校書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era the promotion-and-demotion commissioner Zhao Zan recommended him to the court; he was raised from hermitage, granted probationary collator.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, promotion-and-demotion commissioner Zhao Zan recommended him to the court. He was raised from private life and granted the post of probationary collator.

sentences.zh: 累辟張伯儀、何士幹幕府，進詹事府司直。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly recruited into the staffs of Zhang Boyi and He Shigan and advanced to Rectifier in the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly recruited into the staffs of Zhang Boyi and He Shigan and rose to Rectifier in the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 部官以盜金下獄，滋直其冤，御史中丞韋貞伯聞之，表為侍御史。

translations.literal: A Ministry official was imprisoned for stealing gold; Zi vindicated his innocence; Censor-in-Chief Wei Zhenbo heard of it and memorialized that he be made Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When a Ministry official was imprisoned for stealing gold, Zi cleared him of the charge. Censor-in-Chief Wei Zhenbo heard of it and memorialized that Zi be made attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 刑部、大理核罪人，失其平，憚滋守法，因權勢以請，滋終不署奏。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Punishments and the Court of Judicial Review examined criminals, they lost fairness; fearing Zi's enforcement of law, they used power to request favor, but Zi ultimately would not sign the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Punishments and the Court of Judicial Review examined criminals, they lost impartiality. Fearing Zi's strict adherence to law, they used influence to seek leniency, but Zi ultimately refused to sign the memorial.

sentences.zh: 遷工部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 韋臯始招來西南夷，南詔畢牟尋內屬。

translations.literal: Wei Gao first summoned the southwestern tribes, and Nanzhao's Piluoge submitted to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao first summoned the southwestern tribes, and Piluoge of Nanzhao submitted to the court.

sentences.zh: 德宗選郎吏可撫循者，皆憚行，至滋不辭，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: Dezong selected bureau officials who could pacify and comfort; all feared going; when it reached Zi he did not decline, and the emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong selected bureau officials capable of pacifying and comforting the region. All feared going, but when the choice fell to Zi he did not decline, and the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 擢祠部郎中，兼御史中丞，賜金紫，持節往。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Rites, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, granted gold and purple, and sent bearing the staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Rites with the concurrent title of censor-in-chief, granted gold and purple insignia, and sent bearing the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 逾年還，使有指，進諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After more than a year he returned; the mission had merit, and he was advanced to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he returned. The mission had merit, and he was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞，知吏部選。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and managed selections in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and placed in charge of selections in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 求外遷，為華州刺史。

translations.literal: He sought transfer to the provinces and became prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sought a provincial appointment and became prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 政清簡，流民至者，給地居之，名其裏曰義合。

translations.literal: His government was clear and simple; refugees who arrived were given land to dwell on, and he named the district Yiyi.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was clear and simple. Refugees who arrived were given land to live on, and he named the district Righteous Unity.

sentences.zh: 然專以慈惠為本，未嘗設條教，民愛向之。

translations.literal: Yet he devoted himself to benevolence and kindness as his foundation, never established regulations and statutes, and the people loved and turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he devoted himself above all to benevolence and kindness, never established regulations, and the people loved and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 有犯令，時時法外縱舍。

translations.literal: When there were violations of orders, he often released offenders beyond what the law allowed.
translations.idiomatic: When people violated his orders, he often released them beyond what the law allowed.

sentences.zh: 得盜賊，或哀其窮，出財為償所亡。

translations.literal: When he captured thieves, he sometimes pitied their poverty and paid from his own funds to compensate what had been lost.
translations.idiomatic: When he captured thieves, he sometimes pitied their poverty and paid from his own funds to compensate the victims.

sentences.zh: 召為左金吾衛大將軍，以楊於陵代之。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Grand General of the Left Golden Guard, and Yang Yuling replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Grand General of the Left Golden Guard, and Yang Yuling replaced him.

sentences.zh: 滋行，耆老遮道不得去，於陵使諭曰：「吾不敢易袁公政。」

translations.literal: As Zi departed, the elders blocked the road and would not let him leave; Yuling sent a messenger to explain, "I dare not alter Lord Yuan's policies.
translations.idiomatic: As Zi departed, the elders blocked the road and would not let him leave. Yuling sent a messenger to say, "I dare not alter Lord Yuan's policies.

sentences.zh: 人皆羅拜，乃得去，莫不流涕。

translations.literal: The people all bowed in rows and only then could he leave; none did so without shedding tears.
translations.idiomatic: The people all bowed in rows, and only then could he leave. None did so without tears.

sentences.zh: 憲宗監國，進拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Xianzong oversaw the state, Zi was advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong oversaw the state, Zi was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 劉辟反，詔滋為劍南兩川、山南西道安撫大使，半道，以檢校吏部尚書、平章事為劍南東、西川節度使。

translations.literal: When Liu Pi rebelled, an edict made Zi Pacification Commissioner for the Two Sichuan Circuits and the Western Hannan Circuit; halfway there he was made acting Minister of Personnel, chief minister, and military governor of Eastern and Western Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi rebelled, an edict appointed Zi Pacification Commissioner for the Two Sichuan Circuits and the Western Hannan Circuit. Halfway there he was made acting Minister of Personnel, chief minister, and military governor of Eastern and Western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 是時，賊方熾，又滋兄峰在蜀為辟所劫，滋畏不得全，久不進，貶吉州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels were flourishing; moreover Zi's brother Feng in Shu was held hostage by Pi; Zi feared he could not preserve himself, long did not advance, and was demoted to prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebels were at their height, and Zi's brother Feng in Shu had been seized by Liu Pi. Fearing he could not save himself, Zi long delayed advancing and was demoted to prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙義成節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 滑，用武地，東有淄青，北魏博，滋嚴備而推誠信，務在懷來。

translations.literal: Hua was martial territory; to the east was Ziqing, to the north Wei and Bo; Zi kept strict defenses yet promoted sincerity and trust, aiming to win people over.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was a martial region, with Ziqing to the east and Wei and Bo to the north. Zi maintained strict defenses yet promoted sincerity and trust, aiming above all to win people over.

sentences.zh: 李師道、田季安畏服之。

translations.literal: Li Shidao and Tian Ji'an feared him and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao and Tian Ji'an feared him and submitted.

sentences.zh: 居七年，百姓立祠祝祭。

translations.literal: After seven years the common people erected a shrine and offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years the common people erected a shrine in his honor and offered sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 以戶部尚書召，改檢校兵部，拜山南東道節度使，徙荊南。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Revenue, changed to acting Minister of War, appointed military governor of the Eastern Hannan Circuit, and transferred to Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Minister of Revenue, reassigned as acting Minister of War, appointed military governor of the Eastern Hannan Circuit, and then transferred to Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟之反，滋言蔡兵勁，與下同欲，非朝夕計可下，宜廣方略，離潰其心。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji rebelled, Zi said the Cai troops were strong, shared the same desires as their subordinates, and could not be taken by a plan of a morning and an evening; one should broaden strategy and separate and collapse their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji rebelled, Zi said the Cai troops were strong, shared the same aims as their commanders, and could not be subdued overnight. Broad strategy was needed to divide them and break their morale.

sentences.zh: 及宿兵三年，調發益屈，詔出禁錢繼之。

translations.literal: When the garrison troops had been encamped three years and levies grew ever more strained, an edict issued forbidden treasury funds to continue the effort.
translations.idiomatic: After the garrison troops had been encamped for three years and levies grew ever more strained, an edict ordered forbidden treasury funds released to sustain the campaign.

sentences.zh: 滋揣天子且厭兵，自表入朝，欲議罷淮西事，道聞蕭俯、錢徽坐沮議黜去，滋翻其謀，更言必勝，順可天子意，乃得還。

translations.literal: Zi guessed the Son of Heaven was already weary of war; he submitted a memorial asking to enter court, intending to discuss abandoning the Huai-Xi campaign. On the road he heard that Xiao Fu and Qian Hui had been dismissed for obstructing such a proposal. Zi reversed his plan, instead saying victory was certain, conforming to what would please the emperor, and was then allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Reading that the emperor was growing weary of war, Zi submitted a memorial asking to come to court to discuss ending the Huai-Xi campaign. On the road he learned that Xiao Fu and Qian Hui had been removed for blocking that very proposal. Zi reversed himself, declared that victory was certain, and said what would please the throne—and only then was he permitted to return.

sentences.zh: 俄而高霞寓敗，帝思以恩信傾賊，且滋嘗云云，乃授彰義節度使，僑治唐州。

translations.literal: Soon Gao Xiayu was defeated. The emperor thought to overturn the rebels through grace and trust, and since Zi had once spoken accordingly, he was appointed military governor of Zhangyi, administering provisionally from Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gao Xiayu suffered defeat. The emperor resolved to topple the rebels through kindness and trust; since Zi had already spoken in that vein, he was made military governor of Zhangyi, with his seat provisionally at Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以滋儒者，拜陽旻為唐州刺史，將其兵。

translations.literal: Because Zi was a Confucian scholar, Yang Min was appointed prefect of Tangzhou to command the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zi was a scholar rather than a soldier, Yang Min was appointed prefect of Tangzhou to take command of the army.

sentences.zh: 滋先世墳墓在蔡，吳少陽時為修墓，禁芻牧，諸袁多署右職，稟給之。

translations.literal: Zi's ancestral graves were in Cai. During Wu Shaoyang's time they had been repaired, grazing was forbidden, many of the Yuan clan were given posts on the right, and they were supplied with rations.
translations.idiomatic: Zi's ancestral tombs lay in Cai. Under Wu Shaoyang they had been restored, grazing there was forbidden, many Yuans were given posts on the right wing, and all were kept on stipend.

sentences.zh: 滋至治，去斥候，與元濟通好。

translations.literal: When Zi arrived to govern, he removed scouts and opened friendly relations with Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi took up his post, he withdrew the outposts and entered into friendly communication with Wu Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 賊圍新興，滋卑辭講解，賊因是易滋，不為備。

translations.literal: The rebels besieged Xinxing. Zi spoke humbly to negotiate relief, and the rebels therefore held him in contempt and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels besieged Xinxing, Zi pleaded humbly for a settlement. The rebels took him lightly and ceased to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 時帝責戰急，而滋至六月，以無功貶撫州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was pressing urgently for battle, but by the sixth month after Zi's arrival he had achieved nothing and was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pressing for swift action, yet by the sixth month of Zi's tenure he had accomplished nothing and was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to governor of Hunan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he was transferred to governor of Hunan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 累封淮陽郡公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed cumulatively as Duke of Huaiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly enfeoffed, ultimately as Duke of Huaiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died at seventy and was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy and was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 滋既病，作遺令處後事，訖三年，皆有條次。

translations.literal: When Zi fell ill, he drew up last instructions for his affairs; for the next three years everything was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi fell ill, he set down last instructions for his household; for the three years that followed, everything was carried out in proper order.

sentences.zh: 性寬易，與之接者，皆自謂可見肺肝，至家人不得見喜慍。

translations.literal: His nature was generous and easygoing. Those who met him all thought they could see his inmost heart; yet even his family could not tell when he was pleased or angry.
translations.idiomatic: He was open and easy in temperament. Everyone who met him felt he had nothing to hide, yet even his own household could never read his pleasure or anger.

sentences.zh: 薄居處衣食。

translations.literal: He lived simply in dwelling, clothing, and food.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly in his dwelling, dress, and fare.

sentences.zh: 能為《春秋》，嘗以劉惲《悲甘陵賦》褒善斥惡戾《春秋》指，然其文不可廢，乃著後序。

translations.literal: He was versed in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He once held that Liu Yun's "Lament for Ganling" praised good and condemned evil contrary to the intent of the Spring and Autumn, yet felt the text could not be discarded and so wrote a preface to it.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He once argued that Liu Yun's "Lament for Ganling" praised virtue and condemned wickedness in ways that cut against the Annals' intent, yet judged the work too fine to suppress and wrote a preface for it.

sentences.zh: 工篆隸，有古法。

translations.literal: He was skilled in seal and clerical script, with the antique methods.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in seal and clerical script and wrote in the ancient manner.

sentences.zh: 子均，右拾遺；

translations.literal: His son Jun was Right Remonstrator;
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun served as Right Remonstrator;

sentences.zh: 郊，翰林學士。

translations.literal: Jiao was Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: his son Jiao was Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 趙宗儒

translations.literal: Zhao Zongru
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zongru

sentences.zh: 趙宗儒，字秉文，鄧州穰人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zongru, courtesy name Bingwen, was a native of Rang in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zongru, courtesy name Bingwen, came from Rang in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 八代祖彤，後魏徵南將軍。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Tong was Southern Campaign General of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His eighth-generation ancestor Tong had been Southern Campaign General under Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 父驊，字雲卿，少嗜學，履尚清鯁。

translations.literal: His father Hua, courtesy name Yunqing, loved learning from youth and was upright and uncompromising in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hua, courtesy name Yunqing, loved learning from youth and was known for upright, uncompromising conduct.

sentences.zh: 開元中，擢進士第，補太子正字，調雷澤、河東丞。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Collator to the Heir Apparent, and was transferred to be assistant magistrate of Leize and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Collator to the Heir Apparent, and served successively as assistant magistrate of Leize and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 采訪使韋陟器之，表置其府。

translations.literal: Investigation commissioner Wei Zhi valued him and memorialized to place him on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation commissioner Wei Zhi admired him and memorialized to have him placed on his staff.

sentences.zh: 又為陳留采訪使郭納支使。

translations.literal: He also served as dispatch officer for Chenliu investigation commissioner Guo Na.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as dispatch officer on the staff of Chenliu investigation commissioner Guo Na.

sentences.zh: 安祿山陷陳留，驊沒於賊。

translations.literal: When An Lushan took Chenliu, Hua fell into the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan captured Chenliu, Hua was caught behind rebel lines.

sentences.zh: 時江西觀察使韋儇族妹坐其夫為畿官不供賊，沒為婢。

translations.literal: At the time a clanswoman of Jiangxi governor Wei Yan's clan was condemned because her husband, a capital district official, had not supplied the rebels; she was reduced to a maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a kinswoman of Jiangxi governor Wei Yan was punished because her husband, a metropolitan district official, had failed to supply the rebels, and she was reduced to servitude.

sentences.zh: 驊哀之，以錢贖韋，厚為資給。

translations.literal: Hua pitied her, used money to ransom the Wei woman, and gave her generous support.
translations.idiomatic: Hua took pity on her, paid to ransom the Wei woman, and supported her generously.

sentences.zh: 賊平，訪近屬歸之，時人高其義。

translations.literal: When the rebels were put down, he found her near kin and returned her to them. People at the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, he found her relatives and restored her to them. People of the time greatly admired his conduct.

sentences.zh: 驊以嘗陷賊，貶晉江尉。

translations.literal: Hua was demoted to assistant magistrate of Jinjiang for having once fallen among the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had once been trapped among the rebels, Hua was demoted to assistant magistrate of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 久之，召拜左補闕，遷累尚書比部員外郎。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned and appointed Left Remonstrator, then promoted repeatedly to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Comparison Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled, appointed Left Remonstrator, and eventually rose to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Comparison Bureau.

sentences.zh: 建中初，遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 敦交友行義，不以夷險慁操。

translations.literal: He valued friendship and righteous conduct and did not let ease or peril disturb his principles.
translations.idiomatic: He prized friendship and integrity and would not bend his principles whether in comfort or in danger.

sentences.zh: 少與殷寅、顏真卿、柳芳、陸據、蕭穎士、李華、邵軫善，時為語曰「殷顏柳陸，李蕭邵趙」，謂能全其交也。

translations.literal: In youth he was close to Yin Yin, Yan Zhenqing, Liu Fang, Lu Ju, Xiao Yingshi, Li Hua, and Shao Zhen. People said at the time, "Yin, Yan, Liu, Lu; Li, Xiao, Shao, Zhao," meaning they could preserve their friendships.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was close to Yin Yin, Yan Zhenqing, Liu Fang, Lu Ju, Xiao Yingshi, Li Hua, and Shao Zhen. People said at the time, "Yin, Yan, Liu, Lu; Li, Xiao, Shao, Zhao"—meaning that they kept their friendships intact.

sentences.zh: 驊位省郎，衣食窶乏，俸單寡，諸子至徒步，人為咨美。

translations.literal: Though Hua held a post as a ministry official, his food and clothing were poor; his salary was meager, and his sons had to go on foot. People sympathized and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hua held a ministry post, he lived in want; his salary was thin, and his sons went on foot. People pitied him and praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 涇原兵反，驊竄山谷，病死，贈華州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Jingyuan troops rebelled, Hua fled into the mountains and died of illness. He was posthumously made governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingyuan army mutinied, Hua fled into the hills and died of illness. He was posthumously honored as governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 宗儒第進士，授校書郎，判入等，補陸渾主簿。

translations.literal: Zongru passed the jinshi examination, was appointed collator, rated in the highest class on review, and was posted as registrar of Luhun.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru passed the jinshi examination, was appointed collator, earned the highest rating on review, and was posted registrar of Luhun.

sentences.zh: 數月，拜右拾遺、翰林學士。

translations.literal: Within months he was appointed Right Remonstrator and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was appointed Right Remonstrator and Hanlin Academician.
