sentences.zh: 時，父驊遷秘書少監，德宗欲寵其門，使一日並命。

translations.literal: At the time his father Hua had been transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat. Dezong wished to honor the household and had both appointed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his father Hua had just been made Vice Director of the Secretariat. Dezong wished to honor the family and had father and son appointed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 再遷司勛員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel's Merits Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was next promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel's Merits Bureau.

sentences.zh: 貞元六年，領考功事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan he took charge of the performance-review office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan he took charge of the performance-review office.

sentences.zh: 自至德後考績失實，內外悉考中上，殿最混淆，至宗儒，黜陟詳當，無所回憚。

translations.literal: Since the Zhide era performance ratings had lost truth; inside and outside all were rated upper-middle; top and bottom were confused. When Zongru took over, promotions and demotions were detailed and fitting, without any bending of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhide era, performance ratings had ceased to reflect reality: officials everywhere were marked upper-middle, and distinctions of merit and failure were blurred. Under Zongru, promotions and demotions were exact and fair, with no bending to favor.

sentences.zh: 右司郎中獨孤良器、殿中侍御史杜倫以過黜考，左丞裴郁、御史中丞盧佋降考中中，凡入中上者，才五十人。

translations.literal: Right Department Director Dugu Liangqi and Palace Censor Du Lun had their ratings cut for faults; Left Vice Director Pei Yu and Censor-in-Chief Lu Dian were downgraded to middle-middle. Those who made upper-middle numbered only fifty in all.
translations.idiomatic: Right Department Director Dugu Liangqi and Palace Censor Du Lun were marked down for misconduct; Left Vice Director Pei Yu and Censor-in-Chief Lu Dian were reduced to middle-middle. In all, only fifty men received upper-middle.

sentences.zh: 帝聞善之，進考功郎中。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and approved, and promoted him to Director of the Merits Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this with approval and promoted him to Director of the Merits Bureau.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以本官同中書門下平章事，賜服金紫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, with his existing rank he became Participating Secretary jointly with the Secretariat and Chancellery, and was granted gold-and-purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became Participating Secretary jointly with the Secretariat and Chancellery while retaining his existing rank, and was granted gold-and-purple robes.

sentences.zh: 居二歲，罷為太子右庶子，屏居慎靜，奉朝請而已。

translations.literal: After two years he was dismissed to Right Subprefect of the Heir Apparent's Household, living quietly in seclusion and attending court only on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was removed from office and made Right Subprefect of the Heir Apparent's Household, living in quiet retirement and attending court only as required.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，召見，勞曰：「知卿杜門六年，故有此拜，曩與先臣並命，尚念之邪？」

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and summoned for audience. The emperor comforted him, saying, "Knowing you shut your doors six years, I therefore made this appointment. Long ago I appointed you together with my late minister—do you still remember?
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and summoned to audience. The emperor comforted him, saying, "Knowing that you kept your doors shut for six years, I made this appointment for that reason. Long ago I appointed you on the same day as your late father—do you still remember?

sentences.zh: 宗儒俯伏流涕。

translations.literal: Zongru prostrated himself and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru prostrated himself and wept.

sentences.zh: 元和初，檢校禮部尚書，充東都留守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was acting Minister of Rites and appointed Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was made acting Minister of Rites and appointed regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 三遷至檢校吏部、荊南節度使，散冗食戍二千人。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel and military governor of Jingnan, dismissing two thousand redundant garrison soldiers on the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: After three further promotions he became acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel and military governor of Jingnan, where he dismissed two thousand redundant soldiers kept on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 歷山南西道、河中二鎮，拜御史大夫，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He served the two circuits of Southwestern Shannan and Hezhong, was appointed Censor-in-Chief, and then changed to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Southwestern Shannan and Hezhong, was appointed Censor-in-Chief, and then became Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，詔先朝所召賢良方正，委有司試。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended, an edict ordered that those summoned as Worthy and Upright in the previous reign be examined by the appropriate offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong ascended the throne, an edict directed that those summoned under the previous reign as Worthy and Upright candidates be examined by the regular offices.

sentences.zh: 宗儒建言：「應制而來者，當天子臨問。

translations.literal: Zongru submitted a memorial: "Those who came in response to the imperial summons should be questioned by the Son of Heaven in person.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru submitted a memorial: "Those who came in response to the imperial summons ought to be questioned by the emperor in person.

sentences.zh: 試有司，非國舊典，請罷之。」

translations.literal: Examination by the offices is not the old national practice; I ask that it be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: To have them examined by the offices is not the old national practice. I ask that this be abolished.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校右仆射，守太常卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太常有《五方師子樂》，非大朝會不作。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites had the "Five-Direction Lion Music," performed only at grand court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites possessed the "Five-Direction Lion Music," which was performed only at the greatest court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 帝嗜聲色，宦官領教坊者，乃移書取之。

translations.literal: The emperor was fond of music and women; the eunuch in charge of the Music Bureau sent a letter requesting it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doted on music and pleasure; the eunuch who headed the Music Bureau sent a letter demanding the score.

sentences.zh: 宗儒不敢違，以訴宰相。

translations.literal: Zongru did not dare refuse and complained to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru did not dare refuse and appealed to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 宰相以事專有司，不應關白。

translations.literal: The chief ministers said the matter was exclusively for that office and should not be reported to them.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers replied that the matter lay entirely within that office's jurisdiction and ought not to be referred to them.

sentences.zh: 以懦不職，罷為太子少師。

translations.literal: For cowardice and failure in office he was dismissed to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Judged cowardly and unfit for office, he was removed and made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 太和初，進太子太傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was promoted to Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era he was promoted to Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 文宗召訪政理，對曰：「堯、舜之化，慈儉而已，願陛下守之。」

translations.literal: Wenzong summoned him to inquire about governance. He replied: "The transformation of Yao and Shun was only kindness and frugality; may Your Majesty hold to them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong summoned him to ask about good government. He answered, "The rule of Yao and Shun rested on kindness and frugality alone. I pray Your Majesty will hold fast to them.

sentences.zh: 帝納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 六年，授司空，致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Minister of Works and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Minister of Works and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十七，冊贈司徒，謚曰昭。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-seven. By imperial patent he was posthumously honored as Grand Secretary; his posthumous name was Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-seven. By imperial patent he was posthumously honored as Grand Secretary, with the posthumous name Zhao.

sentences.zh: 宗儒以文學歷將相，位任崇劇，然無儀矩，以治生瑣碎失名。

translations.literal: Zongru rose through literature to general and minister; his posts were weighty and arduous. Yet he lacked decorum and lost reputation through petty money-making.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru rose through letters to posts as general and minister, bearing heavy and arduous responsibility. Yet he lacked proper bearing and lost standing through petty schemes of private gain.

sentences.zh: 竇易直

translations.literal: Dou Yizhi
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yizhi

sentences.zh: 竇易直，字宗玄，京兆始平人。

translations.literal: Dou Yizhi, courtesy name Zongxuan, was a native of Shiping in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yizhi, courtesy name Zongxuan, came from Shiping in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 擢明經，補校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the mingjing examination and was appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the mingjing examination and was appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 十年不應辟，以判入等，為藍田尉。

translations.literal: For ten years he did not respond to summons; rated in the highest class on review, he became assistant magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years he declined summons to office; rated in the highest class on review, he became assistant magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Director of the Ministry of Personnel Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Director of the Ministry of Personnel Bureau.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，進御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 繇陜虢觀察使，入為京兆尹。

translations.literal: From governor of Shan-Guo Circuit he entered the capital as metropolitan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: From governor of Shan-Guo Circuit he entered the capital as metropolitan prefect.

sentences.zh: 萬年尉韓晤坐賕，易直令官屬按之，得贓三十萬，憲宗疑未盡，詔窮治，至三百萬，貶易直為金州刺史。

translations.literal: Wannian assistant magistrate Han Wu was implicated in bribery. Yizhi had his subordinates investigate and found three hundred thousand in illicit gains. Xianzong suspected the sum was incomplete and ordered thorough prosecution; it reached three million, and Yizhi was demoted to prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian assistant magistrate Han Wu was implicated in bribery. Yizhi had his staff investigate and uncovered three hundred thousand in illicit gains. Xianzong suspected the figure was too low and ordered a full inquiry; the total reached three million, and Yizhi was demoted to prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為宣歙、浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was restored as governor of Xuan-She and Zhexi circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was restored to office as governor of Xuan-She and Zhexi circuits.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，李以汴州叛，易直欲出庫財賞軍，或謂給與無名，必且生患，乃止。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing, Li rebelled at Bianzhou. Yizhi wished to distribute treasury funds to reward the troops, but some said payment without proper title would surely bring trouble, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing, Li Tongjie rebelled at Bianzhou. Yizhi wished to open the treasury and reward the troops, but others warned that unaccounted payouts would only breed trouble, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 時江、淮旱，漕物淹積不能前，軍士聞易直向言，其部將王國清指漕貨激眾謀亂。

translations.literal: At the time the Jiang and Huai regions suffered drought; transport goods piled up and could not move forward. Soldiers heard what Yizhi had almost done; his subordinate general Wang Guoqing pointed to the transport goods to incite the crowd to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang and Huai regions were then in drought, and transport goods piled up, unable to move. The soldiers had heard of Yizhi's earlier proposal; his subordinate Wang Guoqing pointed to the transport stores and incited the men to mutiny.

sentences.zh: 易直知之，械國清送獄，其黨數千群歡入獄，篡取之，欲大剽。

translations.literal: Yizhi learned of it, shackled Guoqing and sent him to prison. Several thousand of his partisans stormed the prison together in excitement, seized him by force, and intended to loot on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi learned of the plot, shackled Guoqing, and sent him to prison. Several thousand of his followers stormed the jail in a frenzy, seized him by force, and prepared for a great pillage.

sentences.zh: 易直登樓令曰：「能誅亂者，一級賞千萬！」

translations.literal: Yizhi mounted a tower and issued an order: "Whoever can kill the rebels—ten million for one head!
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi mounted a tower and proclaimed, "Whoever kills a rebel shall receive ten million cash for each head!

sentences.zh: 眾喜，反縛為亂者三百餘人，易直悉斬之。

translations.literal: The crowd rejoiced, turned and bound more than three hundred of the rebels, and Yizhi had them all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd rejoiced, turned on the rebels, bound more than three hundred of them, and Yizhi had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent director of fiscal accounts.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue with concurrent charge of fiscal accounts.

sentences.zh: 四年，同中書門下平章事，轉門下侍郎，封晉陽郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he became Participating Secretary jointly with the Secretariat and Chancellery, was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jinyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became Participating Secretary jointly with the Secretariat and Chancellery, was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery, and was enfeoffed Duke of Jinyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 即讓度支，置其俸三月，有詔停判。

translations.literal: He immediately relinquished the fiscal directorship, setting aside three months' salary; an edict stopped his concurrent duty.
translations.idiomatic: He at once resigned the fiscal directorship, forgoing three months' salary, and an edict confirmed the end of his concurrent charge.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，檢校尚書右仆射、同平章事，為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended, Yizhi was acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Participating Secretary, and military governor of Eastern Shannan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Yizhi was acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Participating Secretary, and military governor of Eastern Shannan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 入為左仆射、判太常卿事。

translations.literal: He entered court as Left Vice Director and concurrent Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Left Vice Director with concurrent charge of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 頃之，檢校司空，為鳳翔節度。

translations.literal: Before long he was acting Minister of Works and military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting Minister of Works and military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 以疾還京師。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒，謚曰恭惠。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Secretary; his posthumous name was Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Secretary, with the posthumous name Gonghui.

sentences.zh: 易直以公潔自喜，方執政，未嘗引用親黨。

translations.literal: Yizhi took pride in public integrity. While in power he never advanced relatives or partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi prided himself on public-minded integrity. While in power he never promoted relatives or faction.

sentences.zh: 初，元和中，鄭餘慶議，仆射上儀，不與隔品官亢禮，易直為中丞，奏駁之。

translations.literal: Early on, in the Yuanhe era, Zheng Yuqing proposed that vice directors in the upper ceremony should not stand on equal ceremonial footing with officials of intervening rank. When Yizhi was censor-in-chief, he memorialized to rebut this.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe era, Zheng Yuqing proposed that vice directors, being of upper ceremonial rank, should not exchange equal courtesies with officials of intervening rank. When Yizhi was censor-in-chief, he memorialized to rebut the proposal.

sentences.zh: 及為仆射，乃自用隔品致恭，為時鄙笑。

translations.literal: When he became vice director himself, he then voluntarily used the intervening-rank ceremony of respect, and people of the time scorned him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When he himself became vice director, he then observed the courtesies due to officials of intervening rank—and contemporaries mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 子紃，仕至渭南尉、集賢校理。

translations.literal: His son Xiu rose to assistant magistrate of Weinan and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiu rose to assistant magistrate of Weinan and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 妻父王涯被禍，宦官知易直子，得不死，貶循州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: When his father-in-law Wang Ya suffered calamity, eunuchs recognized Yizhi's son and spared his life, but he was demoted to revenue adjutant of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his father-in-law Wang Ya met disaster, eunuchs recognized Yizhi's son and spared his life, but he was demoted to revenue adjutant of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：關播舉李元平守汝州，賊縛而臣之。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Guan Bo recommended Li Yuanping to hold Ruzhou; the rebels bound him and he submitted to them.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Guan Bo recommended Li Yuanping to defend Ruzhou; the rebels bound him, and he submitted to them.

sentences.zh: 宰相不知人，果可敗國，德宗不以是責宰相，幾喪天下。

translations.literal: A chief minister who does not know men can indeed ruin the state. Dezong did not hold the chief minister accountable for this and nearly lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When a chief minister cannot judge men, he can indeed ruin the state. Dezong did not hold his chief minister to account for this and nearly lost the empire.

sentences.zh: 晉懦弛茍安，滋欲以恩信傾賊，迂暗之人，烏可語功名會哉！

translations.literal: Jin was lax and sought only ease; Zi wished to overturn the rebels through grace and trust. Men so obtuse and dim—how could one speak to them of occasions for merit and fame?
translations.idiomatic: Jin was weak, slack, and content with safety; Zi wished to topple the rebels through kindness and trust. Men so roundabout and dim—what talk can one have with them of merit and glory?
